name: Wawel Castle
description: A royal castle and cathedral crown a hill above the Vistula in Kraków.

name: Warsaw Old Town
description: Rebuilt historic façades surround the Castle Square and Market Square after wartime destruction.

name: Malbork Castle
description: A vast brick Teutonic fortress on the Nogat river, among the largest castles by area.

name: Neptune’s Fountain
description: A landmark fountain stands on Długi Targ in Gdańsk’s reconstructed main street.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
description: Underground chapels and chambers carved in salt south of Kraków.

name: Tatra National Park
description: Alpine peaks and valleys on the Polish–Slovak border with busy trailheads from Zakopane.

name: Białowieża Forest
description: Ancient woodland shared with Belarus, known for European bison.

name: Sopot Pier
description: A long wooden pier stretches into the Baltic from the resort town of Sopot.

name: Wrocław market square
description: Colourful townhouses ring a large Rynek dotted with bronze dwarf statues.

name: Krupówki Street
description: Zakopane’s main pedestrian street fills with cafés and mountain-gear shops.

name: Sukiennice food & stalls
description: The Cloth Hall’s arcades and nearby stalls sell obwarzanek and regional snacks on the Main Square.

name: Hala Koszyki
description: A restored market hall in Warsaw hosts restaurants and food counters.

name: Oliwa & seaside smoked fish
description: Baltic smoked-fish stands and pier snacks are common along the Tri-City coast.

name: Stary Browar & Old Market eateries
description: Poznań’s old market square and nearby halls offer pierogi and St. Martin’s croissants in season.

name: Lublin Old Town cafés
description: Cafés and regional kitchens cluster in Lublin’s compact historic core.

name: Wianki Festival
description: Midsummer wreath celebrations and concerts by the Vistula, usually around late June.
